references.text: The tithe of everything from the land, whether grain from the soil or fruit from the trees, belongs to the Lord. This establishes the principle of giving a portion to the Lord, which also applies to war spoils in Numbers 31:28.
The Levites were to give one-tenth of the tithe they received as an offering to the Lord. This shows the same principle of lifting up a contribution (תְּרוּמָה) to the Lord from what one receives.
The context for distributing war spoils between the warriors and the congregation, which comes immediately before the instruction about the offering to the Lord.
The continuation explaining that the offering from the warriors was to be given to the priest Eleazar, and a portion from the people's half was to be given to the Levites.
The fulfillment of the command where Moses gave the offering to the priest Eleazar as a gift-offering to the Lord.
Law regarding war spoils that allowed the Israelites to keep women, children, livestock, and everything else in the city as plunder, but shows that a portion always belongs to the Lord.
At Jericho, all silver, gold, and articles of bronze and iron were devoted to the Lord and placed in the Lord's treasury. This illustrates the principle that war spoils partially belong to the Lord.
